What is a key rotation, and why do one?

What a rotation is, and the three reasons we did one.

TraderSwift update1 min readRead Markdown ↗

A rotation moves Signer's work to a new set of machines.

Signer keeps a trading key as shares on separate machines, called signers, and signs an order only if it fits the owner's written limits. How does Signer hold a key? explains it in full.

You rotate when the old machines should no longer be trusted with the key: they're being retired, their setup has a known weakness, or the set needs to grow. Ours did all three.

Before, the launch set was three signers, any two of which could sign, plus a fourth machine that only ran the chain. After, we wanted four machines that each run the chain and sign, any three of which can sign, prepared to a stricter standard.
